---
title: "quarto-index page-range probe"
from: markdown-smart
format:
  pdf:
    # The suite reads the `.ind` makeindex writes, the `.ilg` it logs to, and
    # the `.aux` the typeset-time registry is fed from; Quarto deletes all
    # three on a successful render unless this says otherwise.
    latex-clean: false
    include-in-header:
      # The author redefinition the extension documents, which is also the
      # only way emphasis becomes visible to `pdftotext` at all: `\textbf` and
      # plain text extract identically. Every emphasis claim this fixture
      # makes in the compiled PDF is read through this marker.
      #
      # `\newcommand*`, not `\renewcommand*`: Quarto puts a document's own
      # header text ABOVE what a filter injects, so this definition lands
      # first and the extension's `\providecommand` steps aside.
      text: |
        \newcommand*\quartoindexprincipal[1]{[P:#1]}
  html: default
  # Spans are compared byte for byte, so the writer must not break one across
  # lines at its column limit.
  gfm:
    wrap: none
filters:
  - index
---

# A discussion that spans pages

A term is often discussed across several pages rather than mentioned at one.
`range="open"` and `range="close"` say where such a discussion begins and ends,
and the index prints one locator spanning the two rather than a locator at
each end.

Every range below is separated from its own closing mark by exactly ONE page
holding no mark at all. That separation is what the suite's expectations are
stated over: it makes each range span exactly three pages, so a check can read
the printed range and know what it should be without hard-coding a folio, and
a defect that paired the wrong two marks would print a span of some other
width. Each slot uses a term no other slot uses, so a check reading one entry
cannot be satisfied by another's marks.

The discussion of [alicorn]{.index range="open"} begins here.

{{< pagebreak >}}

A page with no mark on it, inside the alicorn range and holding its two ends
one page apart.

{{< pagebreak >}}

And the discussion of [alicorn]{.index range="close"} ends here.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# A range that is the term's principal discussion

`mention="principal"` on the opening mark says the whole span is the term's
principal discussion, and both ends then carry the same encapsulator —
makeindex warns when they differ, and Quarto fails a render on that warning.
The range prints as one string rather than as a page, so the opening and
closing marks each register their own page and the pair is composed into that
same string in the typeset-time registry.

The principal discussion of [banshee]{.index range="open" mention="principal"}
begins here.

{{< pagebreak >}}

A page with no mark on it, inside the banshee range.

{{< pagebreak >}}

And the principal discussion of [banshee]{.index range="close"} ends here.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# The control this milestone must leave alone

A term marked twice with no `range=` anywhere. Every report this milestone adds
must stay silent on it, both its locators must stay plain and separate, and its
entry must carry no range at all: [centaur]{.index} here,

{{< pagebreak >}}

a page with no mark on it, so makeindex cannot fold the two locators into a
range of its own,

{{< pagebreak >}}

and [centaur]{.index} again here.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# A range on a key that also carries a cross-reference

A range lives in the index tool's encapsulation channel and cannot be moved out
of it. A cross-reference can: where a key carries both, the existing repair
folds the cross-reference into the entry's printed text, exactly as it does for
a plain locator, and the range is left where it is. Both ends emit the same
folded text, so the index tool still sees one key and one range.

The discussion of [dybbuk]{.index range="open"} begins here.

{{< pagebreak >}}

A page with no mark on it, inside the dybbuk range.

{{< pagebreak >}}

And the discussion of [dybbuk]{.index range="close"} ends here.

{{< pagebreak >}}

The cross-reference mark on the same key, which contributes no locator of its
own: [dybbuk]{.index see="centaur"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# A range whose two ends are on one page

makeindex prints a range that opens and closes on one page as that single page,
not as a span of it to itself. The registry is fed both spellings for that
reason — the composed span and the opening page on its own — so a principal
range prints emphasized whichever of the two the index tool chooses.

The principal discussion of [erlking]{.index range="open" mention="principal"}
begins and, in this same sentence and on this same page, ends:
[erlking]{.index range="close"}.
